Another fun training day with my daughter, Lucy! Lucy woke up and asked if I could run her through a workout so of course we hit it.  As a 9 year old, we do a vast mix of training, but this training can be applied to any age (with modifications, of course): Cone game - lateral movement focus. This is a game the kids love and it’s a great warm up. Stand there and throw some cones back and forth while they try to “knock as many as they can” down. They don’t realize the reaction and lateral movement they are creating by simply playing a game!  Sandbag drags (or sled drag) is great for any age. Great from the ground up. If you suffer from knee pain, I highly suggest reverse sledding or reverse treadmill.  Dead hangs.  Amazing for grip strength, spinal decompression, shoulder mobility, back, core. Studies show grip strength is one of the strongest indicators of longevity.  Pushups. Lucy is killing it on the elevated pushups. This set she hit 13 with good form. We have moved her down every week and pretty soon she will be killing them from the floor.  Jumping. By far the best thing for children imo. Requires power and strength, coordination, and deceleration. Power is lost way before strength in adults. Somewhere along the lines adults stop jumping and creating true power and it’s a detriment to our capabilities.  Isometrics. Awesome for any age. Great for joint-angle specificity and muscle growth.  These workouts are not just for my 9 year old. Modifications can be made for any fitness level. Get out there and get after it today! It’s no secret that my time in medicine almost killed me. - And I think the biggest reason why (more than the hours and the exhaustion) was this idea that we’re supposed to accept all of it with a smile. With gratitude. As if the system is doing us a FAVOUR. The 14-hour shifts, 7 days in a row. The mental overwhelm from having urgent 7 tasks competing for your attention. The constant anxiety and fear of making the wrong mistake that could cost a life. The superiors who look straight through you. And then, when you say anything about it, you’re met with: “Oh but how LUCKY are you to be a doctor?” “You’re saving lives, why would you want to do anything else?” That’s the part that really f*cking broke me 😞 I ended up leaving medicine because I just couldn’t take it any longer. And even then, I felt so guilty because of this exact attitude. I thought I was weak, for choosing not to suffer for such a prestigious career. But now that I’ve built a career that I genuinely LOVE and ENJOY every single day… I’ve learnt that suffering SHOULDN’T be a rite of passage. It’s not what makes you a good doctor. It’s not what makes you “worthy” of the title. And it was NEVER supposed to be the price you pay for a career that you love. The more that we say this out loud, and support others who are brave enough to say it too, the louder that calling gets. So, are you with me? 🙏🏽 - P.S.
